description: Operator motions to quickly substitute text objects with register contents, and exchange two text regions. A Lua rewrite of vim-subversive and vim-exchange.
author: gbprod
tagline: Quickly substitute text objects from registers and swap two text regions

options.label: On Substitute Callback
options.description:
Lua function called after every substitution. Receives a params table with a 'register' field containing the register used. Example:

  function(params)
    -- params.register: the register used
  end

Useful for integrating with yanky.nvim: require('yanky.integration').substitute()

options.label: Yank Substituted Text
options.description: When enabled, the text that was replaced during a substitution is pushed into the default register. Lets you swap two pieces of text by substituting one with the other and then pasting what was there.

options.label: Preserve Cursor Position
options.description: When enabled, the cursor stays at its original position after performing a substitution instead of moving to the start of the substituted text.

options.label: Default Text Modifiers
Highlight Substituted Text
options.description: Briefly highlight the text that was just substituted so you can see exactly what changed.

options.label: Highlight Duration (ms)
options.description: How long in milliseconds to show the substitution highlight before it fades out.

options.label: Use Esc to Cancel Exchange
options.description: When enabled, pressing Escape cancels a pending exchange selection. If you disable this, map the cancel function to a key instead (e.g., 'sxc').

options.label: Preserve Cursor Position After Exchange
options.description: When enabled, the cursor stays at its original position after completing an exchange instead of moving to the exchanged text.

options.label: Default Exchange Motion (Lua)
options.description:
Default motion to use for exchange. Plugin default is false (no default motion — user selects via keymap after pressing the exchange key). Set to a motion string like 'iw' to always operate on inner words, or leave as false to require a motion after each keypress.

Example: 'iw'

options.label: Range Substitute Prefix
options.description: The Ex command prefix used for range substitution. Use 's' for the built-in :substitute, or 'S' to use vim-abolish's :Subvert (case-aware substitution).

options.label: Pre-fill Replacement With Current Text
options.description: When enabled, the replacement field in the substitute command is pre-filled with the matched text, giving you 's/word/word/g' to edit instead of 's/word//g'.

options.label: Confirm Each Substitution
options.description: When enabled, Neovim will prompt you to confirm each individual substitution before making the change.

options.label: Match Complete Words Only
options.description: When enabled, the subject text is wrapped in \< \> word boundaries, so 'foo' matches only the whole word 'foo' and not 'foobar'.

options.label: Auto-apply Range Substitution
options.description: When enabled, the substitution is applied immediately without showing the command line for review. Use with caution — there's no chance to adjust the replacement text.

options.label: Command Line Cursor Position
options.description: Where to place the cursor in the command line after opening the range substitute prompt. 'End' places it after the replacement text; 'Start' places it at the beginning.

options.label: Group Substituted Text
options.description: When enabled, the matched subject text is wrapped in a capture group in the generated substitute command, allowing you to reference it as \1 in the replacement. Useful for patterns like 's/\(word\)/prefix_\1/g'.

options.label: Substitute Command Suffix
options.description: String appended to the end of the generated substitute command. Use to add flags like 'g' (replace all occurrences), 'I' (case-sensitive), etc. Leave empty to let the user type flags manually.

options.label: Range Substitute Register
options.description: Register to use as the subject text source for range substitution. Leave empty to use the current word under the cursor. Set to a single character like '"' or '+' to pull from a named register.

options.label: Range Subject (Lua)
Range Definition (Lua)

functions.name: operator
functions.label: Substitute (with motion)
functions.description: Substitute the text object from the next motion with register contents. Dot-repeatable.
functions.whatItDoes: After pressing the key mapped to this function, wait for a motion (e.g., 'iw' for inner word, 'ip' for paragraph) and the selected text is replaced with the default register contents.

functions.name: line
functions.label: Substitute Line
functions.description: Substitute the entire current line with register contents.
functions.whatItDoes: Replaces the whole line the cursor is on with whatever is in the default register.

functions.name: eol
functions.label: Substitute to End of Line
functions.description: Substitute from the cursor position to the end of the line with register contents.
functions.whatItDoes: Replaces everything from the cursor to the end of the line with the default register contents.

functions.name: visual
functions.label: Substitute Visual Selection
functions.description: Substitute the current visual selection with register contents.
functions.whatItDoes: Replaces the highlighted visual selection with the default register contents. Use this as a visual-mode mapping.

functions.name: exchange_operator
functions.label: Exchange (with motion)
functions.description: Mark the first region for exchange, then invoke again to swap with a second region.
functions.whatItDoes: First press marks a text region (e.g., a word). Press again on a different region to swap the two. Dot-repeatable for the second press.

functions.name: exchange_line
functions.label: Exchange Line
functions.description: Mark the current line for exchange. Invoke again on another line to swap them.
functions.whatItDoes: Selects the entire current line as the first exchange region. Then move to another line and invoke again to swap the two lines.

functions.name: exchange_visual
functions.label: Exchange Visual Selection
functions.description: Mark the visual selection for exchange. Invoke again on another selection to swap them.
functions.whatItDoes: Selects the highlighted visual region as the first exchange region. Move to another location, make a visual selection, and invoke again to swap.

functions.name: exchange_cancel
functions.label: Cancel Exchange
functions.description: Cancel a pending exchange selection without making any changes.
functions.whatItDoes: If you have marked the first exchange region but changed your mind, this clears the selection so you can start over.

functions.name: range_operator
functions.label: Range Substitute (with two motions)
functions.description: Open a :substitute command pre-filled to replace the first motion's text across the second motion's line range.
functions.whatItDoes: After pressing the key, select what to replace (first motion), then select the range of lines to apply it to (second motion). The command line opens pre-filled for you to type the replacement.

functions.name: range_visual
functions.label: Range Substitute (from visual selection)
functions.description: Use a visual selection as the subject to replace, then pick a motion for the line range.
functions.whatItDoes: Select the text to replace visually, then invoke and pick a motion to define the range of lines. Opens the command line pre-filled.

functions.name: range_word
functions.label: Range Substitute (word under cursor)
functions.description: Use the word under the cursor as the subject, then pick a motion for the line range.
functions.whatItDoes: Treats the complete word under the cursor as the text to replace. Then pick a range motion (e.g., 'ip' for paragraph). Enforces word boundaries automatically.

functionTemplates.label: Substitute with Motion
functionTemplates.shortDescription: Replace the next motion's text object with register contents
functionTemplates.whatItDoes: Map this to a key (e.g., 's'). After pressing the key, type any motion (e.g., 'iw' for inner word, 'ap' for a paragraph) and that region is replaced with your register contents. Dot-repeatable.

functionTemplates.label: Exchange Text Regions
functionTemplates.shortDescription: Swap two text regions using back-to-back exchange motions
functionTemplates.whatItDoes: Map this to a key (e.g., 'sx'). Press once to mark the first region (e.g., 'sxiw' for a word). Press again on a different region to swap the two in place.
